oneLiner: AMD is now a $1T second source for AI compute - record Q2 2026 results, gigawatt-scale OpenAI/Meta/Anthropic commitments and a guided doubling of data center sales in 2027 leave the stock (~$634, Oct 2, 2026) needing flawless Helios/MI450 execution.
thesis: Data center is compounding at triple-digit rates. Q2 2026 data center revenue of $6.7B grew 107% YoY and is 58% of sales; at Citi TMT (Sep 8, 2026) management said data center should roughly double in 2027 to about $70B, with AI GPUs in the low $40Bs.

The customer roster de-risks the roadmap. OpenAI (6GW, first 1GW of MI450 in H2 2026), Meta (up to 6GW, custom MI450-based part) and Anthropic (up to 2GW of MI450 in Helios, first GW in 1H 2027) are multi-generation anchor customers.

The MI450/Helios ramp is on schedule so far. Per the CFO at Citi TMT (Sep 8, 2026), Q3 2026 marks the start of production shipments and revenue, with a very significant step-up in Q4 2026 and another in Q1 2027.
Agentic AI is reigniting server CPUs. AMD raised its 2030 server CPU TAM to $220B (from $60B) and expects server CPUs to grow 80%+ YoY in 2H 2026 and 70%+ into 2027 (Citi TMT, Sep 8, 2026).

AMD is buying a model layer. The ~$8.2B all-stock World Labs deal (announced Sep 28, 2026, close expected by end-2026) plus the completed Taalas buy aim to give Instinct a workload story beyond 'second source'.

latestProse: Q2 2026 (reported Aug 4): revenue $11.5B, +50% YoY and a record, with non-GAAP gross margin of 56% (+200bps+ YoY), non-GAAP EPS $1.66 (GAAP $1.38). Data center drove everything: $6.7B, +107% YoY, 58% of sales, on EPYC and Instinct. Client rose 23% to $3.1B on record mobile sales; gaming fell 31% to $779M on late-cycle semi-custom. The disclosure that matters most: Helios, AMD's first rack-scale platform, is in production, and second-gen Helios with MI455X begins shipping to Meta and OpenAI in the coming months - the proof point that AMD can sell systems, not just chips. The stock fell ~7% after hours, then rallied ~35% from Aug 20 to Oct 2.
guidanceProse: Q3 2026 guidance of ~$13.0B plus or minus $300M revenue (about +41% YoY) and ~56% non-GAAP gross margin is unchanged since Aug 4. At Citi TMT (Sep 8, 2026) the CFO reiterated the Q3 margin but said Q4 2026 and 2027 gross margin should be slightly lower as MI450 ramps, prioritizing gross-profit dollars and operating leverage. She cited $29-30B of supply purchase commitments with wafers, HBM, packaging and substrates still tight. Bulls point to a ~$70B 2027 data center target; bears note rack-scale GPUs are now explicitly margin-dilutive.

guide.label: Q3 2026 revenue guide
guide.sub: ~+41% YoY at midpoint; non-GAAP gross margin ~56%

segments: Data center: $6.7B, 58% of revenue, +107% YoY (EPYC CPUs + Instinct GPUs)
Client: $3.1B, ~27% of revenue, +23% YoY; Gaming: $779M, ~7%, -31% YoY
competitive: Nvidia still dominates AI accelerator revenue and is already shipping Vera Rubin while Helios is just ramping; AMD's 2026 share is single-digit (exact figure unverified)
AMD claims a tokens-per-dollar advantage in large-scale inference and is expanding training capability with MI450 (Citi TMT, Sep 8, 2026)
Hyperscaler custom silicon (Google TPU, AWS Trainium, Broadcom ASICs) is a larger, faster-growing threat to merchant GPU vendors than AMD is to Nvidia
Versus Intel and Arm: agentic-AI CPU demand lifted all three in Sep 2026; AMD targets ~half of a $220B 2030 server CPU market across instruction sets
Cerebras partnership (Jul 23, 2026) pairs Helios throughput with wafer-scale low-latency decode, and the Taalas buy adds in-house ultra-low-latency inference silicon
moat: AMD's moat is chiplet design execution plus the only complete CPU+GPU+networking rack-scale alternative to Nvidia, reinforced by customers who strategically need a second source. ROCm software remains the soft flank versus CUDA, and the warrant-laced OpenAI structure shows AMD still pays for demand certainty rather than commanding it.
risks: Priced for perfection. Shares rose ~30% in September 2026 to a ~$1.03T cap at ~40x forward earnings; a Helios slip would hit a stock that has front-run 2027.
Margin dilution is now guided. Management said Q4 2026 and 2027 gross margin should dip slightly below 56% as MI450 ramps (Citi TMT, Sep 8, 2026).
Dilution from warrants and M&A. Up to 160M shares issuable to OpenAI as milestones vest, plus a floating share count for the ~$8.2B World Labs deal (about 0.8% of shares at the Oct 2 price).
Supply constraints. Advanced wafers, HBM, packaging and substrates remain tight despite $29-30B of purchase commitments; shortfalls cap the 2027 ramp.
Customer concentration in a circular AI capex cycle. Demand concentrates in a few AI labs and hyperscalers whose financing - OpenAI's especially - is aggressive and unproven.
Execution and regulatory. Helios is AMD's first rack-scale system; World Labs needs unnamed regulatory approvals; China export licensing remains a standing risk.
catalysts: Oct 12, 2026: Lisa Su opening keynote at OCP Global Summit
~Nov 3, 2026 (expected; not yet confirmed by AMD): Q3 2026 earnings - first MI450 revenue, Q4 guide, margin path
Q4 2026: 'very significant' MI450/Helios step-up; first 1GW OpenAI deployment (first warrant tranche vests)
By end-2026: World Labs acquisition close, subject to regulatory approvals
1H 2027: first gigawatt of Anthropic Helios deployment begins; further MI450 step-up in Q1 2027
pricedIn: Shares closed at $633.91 on Oct 2, 2026 (intraday record $645.46), up ~35% from $469.46 on Aug 20 and ~30% in September - a ~$1.03T market cap at roughly 40x forward earnings (~39x at ~$610 on Sep 21 per data snapshot). The price assumes data center roughly doubles to ~$70B in 2027, the gigawatt deals convert on schedule and the guided margin dip stays slight. The debate: is the 2027 target effectively contracted backlog, or is AMD buying share with pricing, warrants and stock-funded M&A so EPS lags the multiple?

scenarios.bear: MI450/Helios slips or HBM/packaging supply caps the Q4-Q1 step-ups; margins dilute more than 'slightly' and OpenAI demand proves financing-constrained. 2027 misses the ~$70B data center target and a ~40x multiple compresses - the stock gives back the September run and more.
scenarios.base: Q3's ~$13B lands in early Nov, Q4 shows the guided MI450 step-up, and data center roughly doubles in 2027 with gross margin a touch below 56%. The stock tracks estimate revisions while the multiple compresses as EPS catches up.
scenarios.bull: Helios becomes the default second-source rack, agentic AI drives server CPUs 70%+ in 2027, and Meta/Anthropic/OpenAI deployments stack through 2027 with World Labs adding a native workload. Data center beats ~$70B and estimates step-change upward.

valPresets.note: At ~40x forward and a ~$1T cap (Oct 2026), even the bear preset needs 15% year-1 FCF growth - the reverse DCF quantifies how much of the ~$70B 2027 data center target is already in the price.
